title: The change management approach
blurb: State the purpose of the change management approach, what it typically contains, where it lives and how it differs from its neighbours.
question: A building society's project board wants to see how staff will be helped to move from the old mortgage system to the new one. Which management product sets this out, and when is it agreed?

teach.h: Purpose of the change management approach
teach.body: Formally, its purpose is to establish the target organizational state needed for the project to meet its objectives, together with how the business will shift from the current state through any interim states. In plain English: it is the project's plan for the people side of the change, saying where the organization must end up and how it will get there.

head: Management approach
Home in the manual
teach.caption: All nine are agreed during initiation and form part of the project initiation documentation (PID).

teach.body: Two content areas come up again and again. First, the characteristics of each state (current, any interim, target), highlighting what changes: routines, practices, processes, culture, responsibilities, structure and capabilities. Second, the enabling activities before, during and after transition, such as consultation, trials, training and a help line.

teach.h: Two headings that are easy to mix up

rows.label: Answers
values: What does each state look like?

teach.caption: A description of how people work today is a current-state characteristic, not an enabling activity.

teach.h: Deciding how much detail it needs
items: The skills and capabilities needed during and after the transition.
Which areas of the organizational ecosystem are likely to be impacted.
The key relationships to be considered.
How best to make the transition.

teach.h: Which approach does this belong in?

teach.body: Larkfield is moving mortgage processing to a new platform. During initiation, project manager Aisha Rahman drafts the change management approach. Under current state she notes that handlers key data twice into two systems; under target state, one entry with automatic checks; under an interim state, new applications on the platform while old cases finish on the legacy system. Enabling activities include consultation with team leaders, trials, training and a help line for the first month.

teach.text: Change management approach vs issue management approach: the first plans the organization's transition to the target state (people element). The second says how issues are captured and how changes to the project baseline are assessed and controlled, including change authority and change budget (issues practice).

items: Purpose: establish the target organizational state and how the business will move there from the current state, through any interim states.
It is one of the nine management approaches and part of the PID.
Typical contents: characteristics for each state; enabling activities before, during and after transition.
Created in 'agree the management approaches' (IP); reviewed at stage boundaries and at closure.
Not the issue management approach, which controls changes to the baseline.

summary: You can now state the purpose of the change management approach, name its two key content areas, and place it in the PID, created in initiation and reviewed at stage boundaries and closure. You can also tell it apart from the communication, issue and benefits management approaches.

A.q: What is the purpose of the change management approach?
options: To describe how issues are captured and how changes to the baseline are controlled
To define the means and frequency of communication across the project ecosystem
To establish the target organizational state and how the business will move to it
To define the actions that ensure outcomes are achieved and benefits are confirmed
A.why: Its purpose is to establish the target organizational state needed for the project to meet its objectives and how the business will shift from the current state, through any interim states (manual 3.2.1).

whyNot.0: That is the purpose of the issue management approach (issues practice).
whyNot.1: That is the purpose of the communication management approach.
whyNot.3: That is the purpose of the benefits management approach (business case practice).

A.q: Which management product includes the change management approach once the project is authorized?
options: The project initiation documentation
The project brief assembled in SU
The project log's daily log record
The outline business case from SU
A.why: The management approaches, including the change management approach, are part of the PID, which the board approves in 'authorize the project'.

whyNot.1: The project brief is assembled in starting up a project, before the management approaches are agreed in initiation.
whyNot.2: The daily log records informal issues and actions; it does not hold management approaches.
whyNot.3: The outline business case justifies the project; the management approaches are separate PID components.

A.q: Which is an example of an enabling activity in a change management approach?
options: A description of the team's current daily routines
Running trials of the new process with the users
A scale for rating the severity of each issue
A schedule of highlight reports to the board
A.why: Enabling activities before, during and after transition include consultation, trials, training and a help line.

whyNot.0: Current routines describe the current state, so they belong under characteristics for each state.
whyNot.2: Severity scales for issues belong in the issue management approach.
whyNot.3: Highlight reporting belongs to progress controls and communication, not enabling activities for transition.

B.q: In which activity is the change management approach first created?
options: Appoint the project management team
Prepare the next stage plan
Authorize the project
Agree the management approaches
B.why: All nine management approaches are created in 'agree the management approaches' within initiating a project.

whyNot.0: Appointing the project management team happens in starting up a project, before the management approaches exist.
whyNot.1: Next stage plans are prepared in managing a stage boundary, where the approaches are reviewed rather than first created.
whyNot.2: In 'authorize the project' the board approves the PID; it does not create the approaches.

B.q:
Which two statements about the change management approach are correct?
1. It is one of the nine management approaches.
2. It forms part of the project initiation documentation.
3. It records each request for change and its current status.
4. It is first created in the closing a project process.
options: 1 and 3
1 and 2
2 and 4
3 and 4
B.why: It is one of the nine management approaches (1) and forms part of the PID (2).

whyNot.0: Statement 3 is false: requests for change are recorded in the issue register.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is false: it is created during initiating a project and reviewed at closure.
whyNot.3: Both are false: requests for change go in the issue register, and the approach is created in initiation.

B.q: A project manager is deciding how much detail the change management approach needs. Which should she consider?
options: Which areas of the organizational ecosystem will be impacted
Which quality methods will be used to check each product
Which scale will be used to rate each risk's probability
Which tolerances will apply to each team's work package
B.why: Considerations include skills needed during and after transition, the areas of the organizational ecosystem likely to be impacted, key relationships, the evolving culture and how best to transition.

whyNot.1: Quality methods are set out in the quality management approach and product descriptions.
whyNot.2: Probability scales belong in the risk management approach.
whyNot.3: Work package tolerances are set by the project manager in work package descriptions.

C.q: A board member asks where she can find how staff will be supported through the switch to a new platform, and when that was agreed. Which answer is correct?
options: In the communication management approach, agreed in starting up a project
In the issue management approach, agreed in initiating a project
In the change management approach, agreed in initiating a project
In the benefits management approach, agreed at the final stage boundary
C.why: Support through transition (enabling activities) belongs in the change management approach, which is agreed during initiating a project as part of the PID.

whyNot.0: The communication approach covers means and frequency of communication; and no management approach is agreed in starting up.
whyNot.1: The issue management approach covers issues and baseline change control, not support through transition.
whyNot.3: The benefits approach covers achieving outcomes and confirming benefits; it is created in initiation, not at the final stage boundary.

C.q: Which entry belongs under 'characteristics for each state' rather than 'enabling activities'?
options: A help line for claims handlers in the month after go-live
Two weeks of hands-on trials before the switch-over
Classroom training for handlers during the transition
Handlers currently key each claim into two separate systems
C.why: How people work today describes the current state, so it is a characteristic of a state.

whyNot.0: A help line supports people after transition, so it is an enabling activity.
whyNot.1: Trials before switch-over are an enabling activity before transition.
whyNot.2: Training during transition is an enabling activity.

C.q: An entry reads: 'Requests to alter the agreed scope of the new platform will be decided by the change authority within a £20,000 change budget.' Where should it be recorded?
options: Change management approach
Issue management approach
Communication management approach
Benefits management approach
C.why: How changes to the baseline are assessed and controlled, including delegated change authority and the change budget, belongs in the issue management approach.

whyNot.0: The change management approach covers the organizational transition, not control of baseline changes.
whyNot.2: The communication approach covers who is communicated with, how and how often.
whyNot.3: The benefits approach covers achieving outcomes and confirming benefits.

reteach.title: A relocation plan for an office
reteach.question: When a company moves office, what plan tells staff what the new office will be like and how they will be helped to move?

blocks.body: A good relocation pack describes the old office, any temporary office, and the new one: desks, routines, who sits where. It also lists the help on offer before, during and after the move: open days, trial runs, training on the new booking system and a help desk. That pack is the change management approach in miniature: characteristics of each state, plus enabling activities.

blocks.text: Changing the agreed floor plan after sign-off is not in the relocation pack: that is change control, which PRINCE2 puts in the issue management approach.

explain.body: The change management approach establishes the target organizational state needed for the project to meet its objectives, and how the business will shift from the current state through any interim states.

test.q: Identify the missing word in the following sentence. The change management approach sets out how the business will shift from the current state through any [?] states to the target state.
options: interim
baseline
approved
delivery
test.why: The purpose statement refers to moving from the current state through any interim states.

whyNot.1: Baselines are approved product versions under change control, not organizational states.
whyNot.2: 'Approved' describes baselined products, not the stepping stones of a transition.
whyNot.3: Delivery stages are management stages, not organizational states.

explain.body: Characteristics for each state show what changes (routines, practices, processes, culture, responsibilities, structure, capabilities). Enabling activities show how people are helped before, during and after the transition.

test.q: Which pair of headings is typical of the change management approach?
options: Stakeholder analysis; communications schedule
Severity scale; use of the change budget
Characteristics for each state; enabling activities
Reasons; expected benefits; expected dis-benefits
test.why: The change management approach describes characteristics for each state and enabling activities before, during and after transition.

whyNot.0: Stakeholder analysis and the communications schedule are communication management approach headings.
whyNot.1: Severity scales and change budget use belong in the issue management approach.
whyNot.3: Reasons and expected benefits are business case headings.

explain.body: Created in 'agree the management approaches' during initiating a project, assembled into the PID and approved when the board authorizes the project. Reviewed at each stage boundary and at project closure.

test.q: After initiation, when is the change management approach reviewed?
options: At each checkpoint held by team managers
At each quality review of a product
In each time-driven highlight report to the board
At each stage boundary and at project closure
test.why: The management approaches are reviewed in managing a stage boundary and in closing a project.

whyNot.0: Checkpoints report work package progress to the project manager.
whyNot.1: Quality reviews check individual products against their quality specifications.
whyNot.2: Highlight reports give the board stage status at set intervals; they do not review the approaches.

explain.body: The communication management approach covers how and how often the project communicates and gathers feedback. The issue management approach covers issues and baseline change control. The benefits management approach covers achieving outcomes and confirming benefits.

test.q: Which management approach defines the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, the project ecosystem?
options: Change management approach
Communication management approach
Digital and data management approach
Commercial management approach
test.why: The communication management approach defines the means and frequency of communication with, and feedback from, across the project ecosystem.

whyNot.0: The change management approach covers the transition to the target state.
whyNot.2: The digital and data approach covers how data and information are created, used and managed (security, privacy, storage, access), not stakeholder communication.
whyNot.3: The commercial approach covers market engagement, procurement and contract management.
